what_this_is: The founder's launch participation record for the composed PetTripFinder production bundle. Read by scripts/pettripfinder/launch_participation.py at assembly time. Every registered market must carry a row; only FOUNDER_AUTHORIZED_FOR_LAUNCH admits a market into the composed bundle. This record never states a market's facts: source readiness is derived by the assembler from the market's own census, partition, policy authority and release contract, and a status that disagrees with the source fails the build. Withdrawing a market here changes no byte of that market's authority and does not affect its own per-market assembly.

decision.reason: Founder authorizes Grand Rapids / Holland to participate in the next production assembly, joining as the ninth market with 43 pet-friendly profiles. Every other market's decision is unchanged: Indianapolis stays authorized as PTF-INDIANAPOLIS-LAUNCH-PARTICIPATION-019 set it, and cincinnati-oh and detroit-ann-arbor-mi remain not source-ready. Grand Rapids was listed NOT_SOURCE_READY by the lineage merge because the assembler could not reach its final partition; 032 fixed the lookup and rebuilt the partition, and this row now records the founder's launch decision.

lineage.what_this_is: Every participation record this one descends from, oldest first, so a deployment authorization can still be matched to the record it signed after more than one reissue. supersedes names only the immediate predecessor; with four reissues behind it that is no longer enough to walk the chain.

decision_basis.what_this_is: What the founder was shown when deciding. These are a RECORD of the basis, not an authority: the assembler derives every one of them from the market's own census, package, shard and release contract, and a status that disagrees with the source fails the build.

final_partition.why_it_is_named_here: 032 rebuilt it from the founder-signed authority. The partition it replaces predates every founder signature this market has and still carried 42 rows as AWAITING_FOUNDER_DECISION.
